learning.javascript:
In JavaScript, you print text using console.log():

console.log("Hello World!");

This writes the text to the console, followed by a newline. It's the most common way to produce output you can see while developing or debugging.
learning.python:
In Python, you print text using the built-in print() function:

print("Hello World!")

Python adds a newline after the text automatically.
learning.cpp:
In C++, you print text using std::cout together with the << stream insertion operator (both come from the <iostream> header, already available in this judge):

std::cout << "Hello World!" << std::endl;

std::endl inserts a newline and flushes the output stream.
learning.java:
In Java, you print text using System.out.println():

System.out.println("Hello World!");

This writes the text to standard output, followed by a newline.
learning.d:
In D, you print text using writeln():

writeln("Hello World!");

This writes the text to standard output, followed by a newline.
